findings.title: Queued future results are dropped when the deadline is reached
findings.why: The loop breaks as soon as `now` is past `submit_by`/`deadline` without draining `self.events`. A finder or verifier future that completed before the deadline but whose callback is still queued is never processed: agent findings are marked incomplete, and a verifier verdict is replaced by the synthetic 'deadline passed' run. If all verifier events are queued this way, the review incorrectly raises 'no finding could be verified'.

findings.title: Event wait ignores submit_by while a verification is pending
findings.why: When both `agents_out` and `checking` are true, the timeout is computed from `deadline`, so `events.get` can sleep past `submit_by` if no event arrives. Slow dimension agents then keep the review in `find_and_verify` until the final deadline instead of being cut off at `submit_by`, consuming the reserve and leaving no time for merge/write.

findings.title: Verifier threads pop checks before waiting for a slot, causing priority inversion
findings.why: Each `verify` task removes a check from `pending` before `run_verifier` waits on `Slots`. With as many verifier workers as slots, lower-priority checks can occupy every verifier thread while waiting for slots. A later blocking/important check stays in `pending` with no thread to pop it, so it cannot become a slot waiter and is delayed behind the lower-priority verifications, violating D-031.

findings.title: Verifier setup failures abort the whole review
findings.why: `UsageMeter(...)` and `verify_priority(...)` are outside the `try` that converts failures to a `VerificationRun`. If they raise, `verify()` raises, and the event loop calls `future.result()` without handling the exception. One verification failure then fails the entire review instead of being recorded as an incomplete verification, contrary to the comment and D-027/D-031.

findings.title: A merged verification keeps the first copy's priority
findings.why: When a same-dimension duplicate joins an existing `_Check`, only `members` is appended; the heap entry and the `Slots` priority remain based on `check.lead.finding.severity`, the first copy. If a later Deep-run copy reports a higher severity, its verification still runs at the lower priority, so a blocking finding can wait behind dimension turns.
